title: Stack Frames
concept: Every time a function is called, it gets its own 'room' on the stack

steps.title: Starting the main Function
steps.explanation:
The main stack frame is created when the program starts.

The key concept in this lesson is observing the LIFO structure where frames are pushed on call and popped on return.

steps.title: Calling funcA (Stack Push)
steps.explanation:
The `funcA();` call pushes funcA's frame on top of main.

Control won't return to main until the called function finishes.

steps.title: Inside funcA: Creating Variable a
steps.explanation:
Local variable `a=10` is created inside funcA's frame.

Local variables are only valid within their function's frame.

steps.title: Calling funcB (Stack Push)
steps.explanation:
The `funcB(a);` call pushes funcB's frame on top.

The value 10 from `a` is copied to parameter `x`.

steps.title: Inside funcB: Creating Variable b
steps.explanation:
The computation `b = x + 1` stores `b=11`.

The funcB frame now contains both `x` and `b`.

steps.title: funcB: Printing the Result
steps.explanation:
`printf` outputs the value of `b` (11).

Output goes to standard output, independent of the frame.

steps.title: funcB Returns (Stack Pop)
steps.explanation:
When funcB ends, its frame is popped and `x`, `b` are destroyed.

Control returns to the caller, funcA.

steps.title: funcA Returns (Stack Pop)
steps.explanation:
When funcA ends, its frame is popped and `a` is destroyed along with it.

Control returns to main.

steps.title: Program Termination
steps.explanation:
`return 0;` terminates main and the last frame is cleaned up.

Summary: function call = push, function return = pop.

quiz.question: If a function recursively calls itself 10,000 times and runs out of stack space, what error occurs?
quiz.explanation: When the stack space (typically 1MB-8MB) is exceeded, no more frames can be pushed, causing a Stack Overflow error.

misconceptions.wrong: funcA's variable a can be used inside funcB
misconceptions.why:
`funcB` can only see variables within its own frame.
`funcA`'s frame is on a different level and cannot be accessed.

keyTakeaway: Function call = stack frame Push, return = Pop. Each function only uses data in its own room (frame).
